summary: One real checkout per foreign channel, taken to paymentGatewayInitialize and stopped there. Shipping resolves, Saleor adds no tax on top of the gross price, and Stripe answers with a LIVE publishable key in all eleven markets.
what_was_written: Eleven checkouts in production Saleor, one per channel. Nothing was paid, confirmed or completed; the script has no mutation that could, and `payment-canary-script.test.ts` fails if one is added. They expire on their own.

no_tax_added_on_top.how: Saleor reported tax 0 in every channel and the total equals the gross line price plus shipping exactly, with each line price read back from that channel rather than assumed — FR and ES price this variant at 92.99 EUR where AT, DE and IT price it at 82.99, which is deliberate price policy and looks like a 10 EUR discrepancy to anyone who assumes one EUR price. Prices are gross with the market's VAT already inside them, which is why this had to be measured: `tax_configuration` in Saleor is still DEFERRED_BY_OWNER, so nothing but a real checkout could show whether Saleor would add VAT a second time.

stripe_initialized.note: Mode only — no key is read, printed or stored by the script.

not_claimed: Nothing here proves a payment. The canary stops at paymentGatewayInitialize by construction: no charge, no confirmation, no order, and no test of what Stripe does with a real card.
One product, one weight band (0-5 kg). A heavier or oversized item may resolve a different shipping method or none at all.
Delivery lead time is a copy claim (5-10 working days in the EU, 7-14 for US and CA, owner decision 2026-09-22), not something this measures.
